According to a new report, Motorola’s next Razr flip phone is getting some major upgrades and a big schedule change, with Motorola Razr (2027) launching early next year.

It has been revealed that android Headlines today published a new set of images of the Motorola Razr (2027), as well as key specs. The device is shown in three colors and apparently carries the codename “Raptor.”.

There are several key spec changes here, including:.

Motorola Razr (2027) is still only set for three Android OS updates and this fresh model is heavier at 195g (likely due to the bigger battery), but Motorola is very clearly making some substantial upgrades here. The biggest change is to the displays, both of which now match the Razr+ and Razr Ultra models. Some key specs, such as 8GB of RAM and 256GB of storage, are unchanged from the 2026 release.

Motorola has been releasing its Razr series in the Spring, but today’s report claims that Razr (2027) will launch in January 2027, likely at CES and at the same time as the Razr Flex book-style foldable. There’s no word on new Plus or Ultra models yet.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that there was once a time when OLED gaming monitors commanded a hefty premium over their IPS- and VA-based competition. However, especially over the past year, prices have dropped low enough that we’re seeing some really compelling prices on OLED monitors. Such is the case for anyone looking to purchase a 27-inch gaming monitor, which you can now find for well under $300. For example, you can get an Acer Predator X27U W1 for $269.99, while the Innocn 2780S is available for $279 at Amazon.

I’ve found a total of four 27-inch QHD monitors that are worth your attention (including the two mentioned above), so without further ado, let's see what’s cooking.

The Acer Predator X27U W1 is a 27-inch gaming monitor with a QHD resolution, 240 Hz refresh rate, and a QD-OLED panel. It supports AMD FreeSync Premium and includes two HDMI 2.1 and two DisplayPort 1.4 ports.

Recent findings suggest that the Acer Predator X27U W1 features a 26.5-inch QD-OLED Penta Tandem panel. Acer claims that the Penta Tandem panel boosts luminous efficiency, doubles panel life, and allows for peak brightness of up to 1,000 nits (although typical brightness is closer to 200 nits).

It has been revealed that you’ll find a 240 Hz refresh rate with support for AMD FreeSync Premium, 0.03 ms GtG response time, 99 percent coverage of the sRGB color space, an anti-glare coating over the display panel, and dual 3-watt speakers. On the connectivity front, you get two HDMI 2.1 ports, two DisplayPort 1.4 ports, and a single 3.5 mm headphone jack. The Predator X27U W1 is also adjustable for height, pivot, tilt, and swivel. The monitor rings up with a 14 percent discount at Amazon, bringing its final price to $269.99.

Recent findings suggest that the Innocn 2780S is a 27-inch gaming monitor with a QHD resolution, 240 Hz refresh rate, and a QD-OLED panel. It covers 99% of sRGB and DCI-P3 and offers peak brightness of 400 nits.

Industry observers note that the Innocn 2780S follows a similar formula with a matte screen finish, 0.03 ms GtG response time, and 99 percent sRGB coverage (and 99 percent for DCI-P3). However, the monitor doesn’t list any official AMD FreeSync Premium or G-Sync certification, only claiming Adaptive-Sync support from 48 Hz to 240 Hz. Innocn lists brightness for the QD-OLED panel at 250 nits typical and 400 nits peak/HDR. You still get two HDMI 2.1 ports and two DisplayPort 1.4 ports, along with a 3.5 mm headphone jack and two 3-watt speakers. The 2780S is now available at 20 percent off, ringing up at $279.99.

The Gigabyte GO27Q24G switches the formula up slightly, instead opting for a 27-inch Micro Lens Array+ White OLED (MLA+ OLED) display. As the counter to popular QD-OLED panels, WOLED panels tend to be brighter across the operating range. Indeed, Gigabyte states that the GO27Q24G offers a typical brightness of 275 nits and can hit a peak of 1,300 nits with HDR content.

Industry observers note that the GO27Q24G is definitely a looker, as it sports a 4-sided borderless design with extremely thin bezels. It also features a RealBlack Glossy, which strikes a good balance between the color-enhancing clarity of a glossy screen coating and the reflection-rejecting characteristics of matte coatings.

Industry observers note that the Gigabyte GO27Q24G is a 27-inch gaming monitor with a QHD resolution, 240 Hz refresh rate, and an MLA+ WOLED panel. It features a RealBlack Glossy display, a 4-sided borderless design, and can hit 1,300 nits peak brightness.

The monitor has AMD FreeSync Premium and Nvidia G-Sync Compatible certifications, along with a maximum refresh rate of 240 Hz. As for ports, you’ll get two HDMI 2.1, one DisplayPort 1.4, one USB-C, and one 3.5 mm headphone jack. However, one thing you won’t find is integrated speakers.

Recent findings suggest that we recently reviewed the GO27Q24G and came away impressed with its value, video processing, and brightness. As our Christian Eberele explained, “Image and gaming experience are every bit the equal of monitors costing twice as much. The GO27Q24G’s Micro Lens Array delivers tremendous brightness, as much as 1,300 nits in HDR mode. It also has nearly perfect viewing angles. Color volume isn’t quite as large as panels with Quantum Dots or Tandem RGB Stripes, but you do get over 96% coverage of DCI-P3.”.

The Gigabyte GO27Q24G is currently on sale for $297.47, representing a 15 percent discount.

The AOC Agon Pro AG276QZD2 is a 27-inch gaming monitor with a QHD resolution, 240 Hz refresh rate, and a QD-OLED panel. It supports AMD FreeSync Premium and Nvidia G-Sync and offers a peak brightness of 1,000 nits.

It has been revealed that finally, we have the AOC Agon Pro AG276QZD2, which is another 27-inch QD-OLED monitor that we reviewed nearly two years ago. The monitor supports AMD FreeSync Premium and Nvidia G-Sync, and has 250 nits typical brightness (1,000 nits peak). It also comes with two HDMI 2.0 ports, one DisplayPort 1.4 port, and a 3.5 mm headphone jack.

It has been revealed that eberle went on to write about the AG276QZD2, stating, “It has a huge color gamut thanks to Quantum Dot tech, which is larger than last year’s AG276QZD. Accuracy comes from a factory calibration that can only be slightly improved with adjustment. It also delivers the best gaming performance available from any monitor with perfect motion resolution and low input lag.”.

If the AOC Agon Pro AG276QZD2 tickles your fancy, you can get it now for $297.49, which is a 15 percent discount.

The Coros Vertix 4 sports sapphire glass and a titanium bezel, including a built-in flashlight for the first time ever.

Industry observers note that coros is best known for its impressively accurate, lightweight smartwatches for runners, but the firm continues to expand with a upcoming rugged Vertix model. The Coros Vertix 4 sports a 1.47-inch LTPO AMOLED touchscreen display with 3,500-nit peak brightness, sapphire glass for protection, a titanium bezel for added durability, and an operating range of -30 to 50 degrees Celsius (seriously).

In a recent development, the Coros Vertix 4’s built-in flashlight is a first for the firm’s smartwatches and comes after years of fans begging for such a feature. Coros claims it specifically positioned the light toward where your hands are working, making it more than just a fun, niche feature. As with all Coros watches, this one sports weeks-long battery life, rated at 30 days of normal use and even including 105 hours of GPS tracking per charge.

Recent findings suggest that the Coros Vertix 4’s new processor can render offline maps in vivid detail, including landform, road, contour line maps, and satellite maps. 64GB of onboard storage should be more than enough to hold all your tunes (and offline maps), and a 4th-generation optical heart rate sensorwith SpO2 capability will give you great health insights along the way.

The Coros Vertix 4 acts as a “consolidation” of previous Vertix lines, mashing together the disparate features of the Vertix 2 and 2S, all in a 14% slimmer body. All the fan-favorite Coros features are here, too, including a boatload of tracked sports modes and free workouts and training from Coros coaches and athletes. The Vertix 4 also ships with both silicone and nylon bands, so you don’t have to buy extra stuff. The watch ships in black and silver colorways for $799.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Wyze is today launching the Window Bird Cam, a latest $70 camera that has a bird feeder and can identify bird species, keep a log, and more.

The Wyze Window Bird Cam comes in two parts. There’s a stick-up camera that mounts to the inside of your window with a shade to reduce reflections, similar to the Wyze Window Cam that rolled out last year. The other half mounts to the outside of your window with suction cups and includes a tray for birdseed.

The idea here is to attract birds direct to the camera’s view, with Wyze further adding a latest “Bird Watch” feature to its app which can identify bird species and keep a log of what species have stopped by and how many birds are using the feeder.

The camera’s lens is tuned for focus distances of around 4-6 inches and has a higher frame rate of 30fps. The feeder tray has drainage and there’s an add-on perch for $15 extra.

Sources indicate that “Bird Watch” is free for 3 months, but costs $6.99/month (or $69.99/year) after that. Free consumers still get live view and bird detection, but no species ID, a limited log, and no cloud recordings of bird visits (there is a microSD card slot for local recording).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Users are seeing the option to mute a video appear in the YouTube app on Android, but it isn’t showing up for everyone.

In a recent development, screenshots of a latest video control button have started appearing on Reddit over the last week. The posts haven’t exactly begun hot debates, but it’s an interesting UI change. A mute button now sits next to the fullscreen option in the left section of the video player. Tapping it does nothing other than cut audio, until it’s tapped again to unmute.

In a recent development, one user details the app version on their Pixel 11 Pro XL – version 21.46.522. They also note that other devices they’ve checked on the YouTube app versions don’t appear to show any sort of mute button in the UI. Without many comments on either post, it’s hard to nail down just how wide this rollout might be.

In reality, this seems like a very small UI design test for the YouTube app. YouTube will often select a small number of customers to push experimental features to while they polish them further before release. Unlike features that Premium users get to test, these are locked.

It’s not necessarily a substantial change, but it’s sort of a confusing one. One wonders why a mute button is necessary. It also adds another button to accidentally hit when trying to tap the fullscreen option.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Today, we are introducing on-device Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) and Text-to-Speech (TTS) capabilities in Google AI Edge Gallery.
  • This release brings together major advancements across both Google’s system speech models and the open-weight ecosystem:.
  • Below, we’ll explore how this local voice pipeline powers the fresh XR (Extended Reality) Language Teacher showcase, upgrades AI Chat in Google AI Edge Gallery, and how you can build with these APIs and models today.

Today, we are introducing on-device Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) and Text-to-Speech (TTS) capabilities in Google AI Edge Gallery. Voice is often the most natural way to interact with AI on phones and wearables. Recent advances in compact speech architectures now make it possible to run accurate, multilingual ASR and expressive TTS models entirely on device, all within a small memory footprint, with low latency, and completely offline. By pairing these lightweight speech models with on-device small language models (SLMs) like Gemini Nano and Gemma 4, developers can build apps that stream live transcriptions as the user speaks and synthesize natural spoken replies locally.

This release brings together major advancements across both Google’s system speech models and the open-weight ecosystem:.

Below, we’ll explore how this local voice pipeline powers the fresh XR (Extended Reality) Language Teacher showcase, upgrades AI Chat in Google AI Edge Gallery, and how you can build with these APIs and models today.

Learning a language while traveling happens in the real world, often in underground stations, busy markets, or abroad where Wi-Fi and roaming data may not be available. To show how vision, language, and speech models can work together 100% locally on your phone with no network connection needed, we built the XR Language Teacher showcase in Google AI Edge Gallery. Simply point your camera at an unfamiliar object or menu, ask "What is that, and how do I ask for one?", and immediately hear an explanation in your language alongside authentic pronunciation in the local language.

Email remains an vital communication channel for web applications. From account verification and password resets to product announcements and customer notifications, many applications depend on email to keep people informed.

For developers, however, implementing email functionality involves more than connecting a service and sending a message. A reliable email system needs to handle authentication, dynamic content, delivery failures, user preferences, event tracking, and integrations with other application components.

Recent findings suggest that using an email service provider (ESP) can simplify this process. Most modern providers offer REST APIs, SMTP relays, templates, automation features, and reporting tools that developers can integrate into existing applications.

This guide explores the technical considerations involved in building email integrations, including API-based sending, webhook handling, automation workflows, and deliverability.

There are two common ways to connect an application to an email delivery service: SMTP and REST APIs.

SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is a standard protocol used to transfer email messages between servers. Developers can connect an application to an SMTP server using credentials and configuration settings.

In a recent development, REST APIs provide another approach. Instead of communicating through an email server protocol, an application sends HTTP requests to an endpoint. The provider processes the request and returns a response.

Both methods can support transactional and application-generated emails, but their implementation differs.

An application already supports SMTP configuration.

Developers want a relatively straightforward integration.

Existing frameworks or libraries provide built-in SMTP support.

An application needs programmatic control over email operations.

Developers want structured responses and error handling.

Email functionality needs to integrate with other application services.

The system requires event tracking or additional API capabilities.

The right approach depends on the application's architecture, expected email volume, and integration requirements.

An API integration allows an application to trigger emails in response to specific events.

For example, an ecommerce application might send an order confirmation after a successful payment. A SaaS application could send an account verification message after registration.

A typical integration follows this process:.

The application detects an event.

The backend prepares the recipient and message data.

The backend authenticates with the email provider.

The provider processes the request.

The application records the response and handles any errors.

Consider a Node.js application that needs to trigger an email campaign through an API.

Some platforms, including Mailmodo, provide REST API functionality for triggering campaigns and integrating external applications with email workflows.

The following example demonstrates the general structure of an HTTP request using a campaign-triggering endpoint:.

According to recent reports, this example uses the documented Mailmodo trigger endpoint and request structure. The campaign ID and API key must be replaced with the values from the relevant account.

Notice that the API key is loaded from an environment variable rather than written directly into the source code.

This is an notable security practice. Credentials should never be exposed in frontend JavaScript, public repositories, or client-side application bundles.

It has been revealed that not every email provider offers the same integration capabilities. Developers should evaluate providers based on their API documentation, authentication methods, supported endpoints, event notifications, and integration flexibility.

For example, Elastic Email provides a REST API that developers can use to send emails and manage different email operations from an application.

In a recent development, its API uses HTTPS requests and API-key authentication. Developers can use the available endpoints to send messages, manage campaigns, retrieve information, and configure webhook notifications.

When evaluating an email API, consider these technical requirements:.

Authentication: Check how API keys are generated, stored, restricted, and rotated.

Documentation: Look for clear endpoint descriptions, request examples, response formats, and error codes.

SDK availability: Official libraries can reduce the amount of integration code required.

Permission management: Separate credentials for sending emails and accessing account information can reduce unnecessary exposure.

API limitations: Review connection limits, request timeouts, rate limits, and account-level restrictions before deploying an integration.

Recent findings suggest that A provider with extensive features is not necessarily the best option for every project. The notable consideration is whether its API supports the application's actual requirements.

Recent findings suggest that sending an email is only one part of the communication process. Applications may also need to know what happens after a message is submitted.

This is where webhooks become useful.

A webhook allows an external service to send an HTTP notification to an application when a particular event occurs.

Depending on the provider, events may include:.

For example, an application could receive a delivery-failure notification and update the corresponding email record in its database.

A basic Express.js webhook endpoint might look like this:.

It has been revealed that this is a simplified example rather than a complete provider-specific webhook implementation. A production endpoint should validate the provider's signature or other authentication mechanism and follow its documented payload structure.

Sources indicate that it should also handle duplicate events safely. Webhook providers may retry notifications when an application does not respond successfully.

An idempotent event handler prevents the same notification from creating duplicate database updates or triggering repeated actions.

Email automation connects application events with predefined communication sequences.

Instead of manually sending every message, developers can create workflows that respond to user activity.

Consider a SaaS application with the following registration process:.

The backend stores the fresh user.

A verification email is triggered.

If the user does not complete onboarding, a follow-up message may be triggered.

A simplified workflow can be represented as:.

In a production application, email delivery should generally be handled through a background job queue rather than blocking the registration request.

A queue also makes it easier to retry temporary failures, manage sending volume, and prevent email delays from affecting the main application.

Developers should consider tools such as Redis-backed queues or framework-specific job processors when building larger systems.

Sources indicate that automation platforms can also help manage more complex journeys. For instance, a developer can connect application events to an external email workflow instead of implementing every communication sequence independently.

The key is to keep business logic in the application while using the email service to manage message delivery and relevant campaign operations.

A successful API response does not necessarily mean that an email has reached the recipient's inbox.

Email deliverability depends on several technical factors, including domain authentication, sender reputation, message quality, and recipient engagement.

Developers should pay attention to the following configurations.

Sender Policy Framework identifies the mail servers authorized to send messages on behalf of a domain.

A correctly configured SPF record helps receiving servers evaluate whether an email originates from an authorized source.

Sources indicate that domainKeys Identified Mail adds a cryptographic signature to outgoing messages. Receiving servers can use the corresponding public key in DNS to verify the signature.

Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance builds on SPF and DKIM. It allows domain owners to publish policies for handling messages that fail authentication checks and receive reports about authentication activity.

These three mechanisms should be configured carefully, especially when an application sends emails through multiple providers.

It has been revealed that email systems generate useful operational data. However, developers should avoid treating every available metric as an accurate measure of user engagement.

For example, open tracking can be affected by privacy features and automated image loading. Click tracking may also include automated security scans.

More reliable application-level signals can include:.

These events can be connected with email campaign data to understand how communication affects application activity.

According to recent reports, developers should also maintain a clear separation between email delivery records and user account records. This makes it easier to investigate delivery issues without unnecessarily modifying customer data.

When collecting engagement information, applications should follow applicable privacy requirements and respect user communication preferences.

Before deploying an email integration, developers should review the following areas:.

API security: Store credentials in environment variables or a dedicated secrets manager.

Domain authentication: Configure SPF, DKIM, and DMARC.

Error handling: Account for failed requests, invalid recipients, and temporary provider errors.

Background processing: Use queues for asynchronous email delivery.

Webhook validation: Verify incoming notifications and handle duplicate events.

Monitoring: Track delivery failures, bounce rates, and application-level outcomes.

Testing: Test email templates across different clients and devices before production deployment.

These practices help create an email system that is easier to maintain, troubleshoot, and scale.

Email integration is an important part of modern application development, but a reliable implementation requires more than connecting an SMTP server or calling an API endpoint.

Developers need to consider authentication, asynchronous processing, webhook security, automation logic, domain configuration, and event monitoring.

REST APIs are useful for applications that need programmatic control over email operations, while SMTP remains a practical option for systems that already support standard mail-server connections. Webhooks add another layer by allowing applications to respond to delivery events and update their internal records.

By choosing an integration method that fits the application architecture and following sound security and deliverability practices, developers can build email functionality that supports both immediate communication needs and long-term application growth.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that if you’re looking for a decent replacement for an older phone or a backup, and the Pixel 10 looks eerily similar to the Pixel 11, is it still worth it? Well, of course it is, but let’s get into why in this deep dive.

One of the best things about the Pixel 10 is that it looks almost identical to the Pixel 11; in some cases, it’ll work with the accessories for the newest phone – but check that before you try. So that means you’re not getting a majorly out-of-date design.

That doesn’t matter to most people, but it could be vital to you. Pixelsnap magnetic accessories still work, and while the Pixel 11 trimmed down the camera bar to an all-glass visor, the overall footprint is virtually identical.

Using the same formula might be stale to some people, but it works, so why change it for the sake of it?

It has been revealed that I’d argue that the best news is that this finally shows Google is confident, given its success with the Pixel 9 and 10 design. The tech giant may make changes in the future, but it’s a fairly solid design that feels great after they settled on a physical form factor that works after years of fiddling, and it’s no secret that the goal is to make the switch from iOS to Android as “easy and painless” as possible. A familiar design goes a long way to calming the nerves of a potential switcher. The Pixel 10 is a perfect example of this philosophy. The Pixel 11 essentially proves that too.

Over a year on from release, there don’t seem to be any major or widespread reports of issues on the Pixel 10. I’d say that is a good omen, as people will often know within that timeframe if there are quality control issues and problematic hardware faults.

According to recent reports, that mentioned, the only problem I think you have to deal with is the base 128GB storage configuration. It’s not insignificant, but still not going to be tons of room for everything. If you take lots of photos and download loads of things locally to your device, then maybe go for the 256GB model.

One of the weirdest things about the Pixel 10 was that after the Pixel 11 launched along with all other supported handsets, it had a newer version of Android than the latest phone.

Yes, you read that correctly: the Pixel 10 had QPR1 before the Pixel 11.

It has been revealed that the entire experience is just more of the same goodness that started with the addition of Material 3 Expressive last year. Android 17 keeps improving; the quality-of-life changes make for a really compelling experience that, while taking some cues from iOS, hasn’t gone full Liquid Glass. Google hasn’t quite kept the day-one enhancement promise like the old days of Pixel, but you still have the cutting edge of the software. Even the Galaxy S26 series isn’t running a release this new and probably won’t for a while.

Rambler has even been added recently, so there is a function bleeding down from the Pixel 11, and there are loads of other quality-of-life changes and features that came with Android 17 QPR1 thrown in. Any bugs that might have been there, however limited, have been addressed in the year the phone has been around.

With the Pixel 10, you may miss out on some of the extra Gemini Intelligence perks or a couple of visual gimmicks like the Pro’s HiLight glow, but none that is yet groundbreaking enough to be drastically upset about.

Sure, the competition might offer a faster processor or newer silicon, but can they offer the fluidity of a system that is fully integrated into all parts of your digital life? That’s what the Pixel 10 delivers.

Industry observers note that as I noted, the Pixel 10 has already seen multiple updates, smoothing out early thermal quirks and optimizing battery efficiency. These monthly security patches and Pixel Drops are a testament to the fact that your phone is a constantly evolving product.

With more updates due very soon, the prospect of an even more optimized experience, and many of the best bits of Google all rolled into one handset, it’s a damn good buy, especially as other OEMs are still struggling to get their own Android 17 updates out in a timely fashion. We’re several months on from the full launch, and barely anyone outside of Samsung has offered a wide rollout. Of course, all Pixel 10 devices get day-one updates, with six years of support still left on the clock.

There is one sore point on the base Pixel 10 that I think might make it hard to recommend over the Pixel 10 Pro. The main camera is the same as the Pixel 9a and the 10a on the base 10. It makes it harder to suggest if you care about camera quality.

It’s still super reliable and does take great photos, but it might not be the best in class like previous generations may have been. In fact, I’d go so far as to say that while it’s great you get a telephoto zoom lens, the lower-quality main sensor diminishes it somewhat.

Most people will be better off with the Pro because it has a lot more to work with, but the cameras are still very good on the Pixel 10 and are backed by Google’s excellent updates.

It has been revealed that even video quality stacks up, though I will say Google’s reliance on Video Boost as a workaround for lower-quality footage is a bit of a cop-out. However, it’s a good workaround, and the resulting footage is still excellent, even if I’m hoping for better on-device processing in future Pixel generations.

According to recent reports, ultimately, the camera is a prime example of the Pixel value proposition. You don’t need the absolute latest, greatest, multi-lens Pro Max Ultra setup to take amazing photos. You need a Pixel. The camera on the 10 series is still right up there with the best from Samsung, OnePlus, and others. It’s doing just as much with technically much less.

Sources indicate that the biggest reason that many people who are looking for a latest phone might want to consider at least the Pixel 10 lineup is that, with discounts, you’re getting a great deal — especially since Google bumped the entry price on the Pixel 11. Sure, bigger, better, faster, and shinier phones exist. They don’t give you the same experience, though. You’re paying for something that others can’t replicate, even at higher price tags.

With more updates due very soon, the prospect of an even more optimized experience, and many of the best bits of Google all rolled into one handset, it’s a damn good buy.

Industry observers note that is the Pixel 10 the best option for a phone right now? Suppose you want arguably the best software and are willing to forgo a few of the bells and whistles. In that case, it is an excellent alternative for anyone looking to save a little money without sacrificing too much. It’s a better buy than the Pixel 10a for most people, in my opinion, and you’ll be hard-pressed to find a more compelling mix of software intelligence and hardware value.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

In a recent development, weekly. Free. One click to leave.

It has been revealed that 7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

Your accessibility check in CI is green. axe-core ran, zero violations, and the badge in the README looks great. Your site can still fail WCAG 2.2.

Recent findings suggest that that isn't a bug in axe. WCAG 2.2 became a W3C Recommendation in October 2023. It added nine success criteria and dropped one (4.1.1 Parsing), and most of the new ones can't be judged by reading the DOM. Deque said as much when it shipped the first WCAG 2.2 support in axe-core 4.5: the target-size rule would probably be the only new-criterion rule they added, because the others can't be automated without a lot of false positives.

So the rest is on you. This article covers the one criterion axe can check and three it can't (focus not obscured, dragging movements, accessible authentication), with Playwright tests you can drop into a project. I ran all of them against a small test page that fails every criterion on purpose, and against a fixed version of the same page. If you want a plain-language rundown of every change first, WCAG 2.2 vs 2.1 goes through them. Here I only care about what you can put in a pipeline.

Industry observers note that level A and AA are what most contracts and laws point at, so those are the ones that matter first. The AAA criteria are still worth knowing about.

Recent findings suggest that that's four AA criteria with something you can script, one of which axe already handles. The rest of this article goes through those four.

The AA rule is smaller than most people expect: a pointer target should be at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, or sit far enough from its neighbours that a 24px circle centred on it wouldn't overlap another target or that target's own circle. There are exceptions, including inline links in a sentence, and targets whose size the browser controls.

axe-core has a target-size rule for this. One catch: it isn't part of a default run. In my setup (axe-core 4.14.1 through @axe-core/playwright 4.14.0), a plain analyze() on the broken page reported nothing at all. The rule only indicated up once I asked for it:.

On the broken page this lists the three 16px toolbar buttons by selector. On the fixed page, with 32px buttons, it passes. If you've been running axe for years and never seen a target-size result, this is why.

According to recent reports, some context on how common the problem is. In the scan data behind my last SitePoint article, 34.5% of the 1,025 sites had controls below a stricter 44px threshold. That is a tougher standard than the 24px that AA asks for, so don't read it as "a third of sites fail 2.5.8". Plenty of those would pass. But it does show how many production sites ship tiny controls.

If you'd like a quick look at one page before wiring anything up, browser tools such as axe DevTools, WAVE, or a WCAG checker will show the same thing.

axe can't test it, because you have to press Tab and look at where the browser scrolled. Two details caught me out building this:.

The check below samples a grid of points inside the visible part of the focused element and asks the browser what's on top at each one. If none of the points land on the element or its children, it's covered.

On my broken page it reported nine hits: links hidden behind the footer going forward ("Section 4 link", "Section 10 link", "Section 16 link") and the toolbar buttons and a few links hidden behind the header coming back. The output names the element and the key, which is what you want when you're staring at a failed build.

The fix is one CSS rule, sized to your sticky elements:.

That tells the browser to leave room when it scrolls a focused element into view. With it in place the same test passes.

Be aware of what this can't see: a modal that opens over the page, or a chat widget that only appears after a delay, will not show up unless your test opens or waits for them. Adrian Roselli's piece on 2.4.11 and adversarial conformance is worth reading for the awkward cases.

According to recent reports, anything you can do by dragging needs a way to do it with a single click or tap, unless dragging is essential. Sortable lists, sliders, kanban cards, file reorderers: all of them.

According to recent reports, you can't prove a drag alternative works from a script. But you can catch the obvious mistake, which is a draggable item with no button anywhere near it:.

The limit is real. It only recognises the native draggable attribute. Libraries built on pointer events, such as dnd-kit, don't set it, so this test will walk right past them. If you use one of those, replace the selector with whatever your component renders, or add a test per drag component. Treat it as a tripwire for the common case, not a verdict.

The fix, in the fixed page, is a pair of "Move up" and "Move down" buttons on each item, each with an accessible name that says which item it moves.

Recent findings suggest that this dispatches a synthetic paste event and checks whether anything called preventDefault() on it. It catches the old onpaste="return false" trick, and it catches script-based blockers too. It does not tell you whether your login has a CAPTCHA that needs an alternative, or an emailed one-time code you must retype. Those need a person.

On a pull request, a plain GitHub Actions job is enough:.

Point PAGE_URL at a running preview, and run the tests against the pages that matter most: sign-in, checkout, anything with a sticky element. Don't try to crawl everything on the first pass. A test that fails for reasons nobody owns gets deleted within a month.

Four things I haven't tried to automate, and wouldn't:.

Automation will keep the regressions out. It won't tell you the work is finished. A green build and a conformant site are different things, and WCAG 2.2 widened the gap between them.

The tests and both test pages are small enough to read in one sitting. Copy what's useful, change the selectors, and keep the broken page around: it's a handy way to check that a test fails when it should.

A2UI 1.0: Build delightful, fast, reliable, agentic experiences

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (318 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Googleblog

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • User interactions with agents today are where computers were in the terminal era: capable, and answering almost everything in text.
  • Recent findings suggest that today, we're releasing A2UI 1.0, the first stable version of our open protocol for generative UI.
  • In a recent development, with A2UI, the agent describes what to show, and every app draws the UI with its own native components.

User interactions with agents today are where computers were in the terminal era: capable, and answering almost everything in text. Users can ask an agent for anything by typing or talking, and what comes back is usually a wall of text, a poor way to compare three products or edit and approve a detailed plan.

Recent findings suggest that today, we're releasing A2UI 1.0, the first stable version of our open protocol for generative UI. It lets AI agents answer with interactive screens, such as a form to confirm or a chart. Developers can use it now with open-source renderer SDKs for the web, Android, and iOS and agent SDKs for Python, TypeScript, and Dart. Companies such as Atlassian, Alation, Bloomberg, and ByteDance are already building with it.

In a recent development, with A2UI, the agent describes what to show, and every app draws the UI with its own native components. The application receives A2UI messages and each app renders the content securely and at native speed. Consumers get the same low latency, high trust, and complete native fidelity whether they reach a manufacturer's agent in its own app or in a third-party AI assistant that hosts MCP apps, such as Gemini or Claude.

According to recent reports, you wake up sick. Getting through the morning takes six apps: book a video visit, move your meetings, tell your team, turn on an out-of-office reply, ask your partner to do school pickup and order soup. Ask a text-only agent instead, and you get a numbered wall of text, then round after round of “which ones?”. A2UI won't handle your sick day, but it gives developers the framework to build an agent that can. That agent could answer with one view of all six apps. Changing your blueprint is a couple of taps instead of another round of messages, and nothing is sent until you confirm.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

A few years ago, renting a VPS meant signing up to be a part-time sysadmin. You’d SSH into a blank Ubuntu prompt and lose a Saturday to Nginx configs and firewall rules before writing a single line of your actual project.

In 2026, three things have changed. What we build has changed: AI coding tools turn weekend ideas into working apps, and AI agents need a machine that stays on after your laptop closes. Who runs servers has changed: you can now ask an AI agent in your terminal to set up a reverse proxy, close a port or work out why something broke. And what servers cost has changed: the AI boom is soaking up the world’s memory supply, and hosting prices are rising with it.

So I bought the smallest Hostinger VPS plan, deployed a Node.js app in Docker, and handed the DevOps work to Hostinger Agent, the AI assistant built into the dashboard.

Below is what that felt like step by step and whether it’s worth locking in a price before they climb further.

Most VPS hosting for developers now falls into four buckets. They all run on the same kind of machine; what changes is how much RAM you give them.

Industry observers note that apps built with AI coding tools. Claude Code and Cursor get you to a working Node.js or Python app fast, then leave you wondering where to put it. A VPS gives you one fixed monthly bill instead of usage-based pricing. If you want push-to-deploy, Hostinger offers Ubuntu templates with Coolify or Dokploy preinstalled.

Recent findings suggest that AI agents and automations that run 24/7. For most people, a “VPS for AI” means a CPU box that never sleeps, not a GPU. Think n8n workflows, a scheduled scraper, or your own agent in a Docker container. Hostinger even has an “Ubuntu 24.04 with Claude Code” template: SSH in, run claude /login, and the agent keeps working after you close your laptop.

APIs, backends and databases for side projects. A Postgres instance, a Redis cache and a small API behind a reverse proxy fit comfortably on a mid-sized initiative. You pick the versions, the extensions and the backup schedule.

According to recent reports, client sites and stores. Freelancers outgrow shared hosting when one client needs a custom PHP extension or a WooCommerce store starts to crawl. A VPS with cPanel or Plesk, or a WordPress or WooCommerce template, keeps client work isolated and under your control.

If you’d rather not build anything from scratch, the Docker Manager catalog listed 1,017 one-click templates when I checked, including 93 under AI/ML and 162 under Developer tools.

In a recent development, for this Hostinger VPS review, the question I cared about was simple: how long from “Choose blueprint” to an app on the internet? On KVM 1, the entry plan, it was about 12 minutes. Here’s each step with rough timings.

In a recent development, I went with KVM 1: 1 vCPU, 4 GB RAM, 50 GB NVMe storage and 4 TB of bandwidth. On the Black Friday deal it costs $6.49/mo, paid upfront as $155.76 for 24 months, and renews at $11.99/mo.

You choose the server’s location and what to install during checkout, alongside your billing details. The location picker shows estimated latency for each data centre; mine highlighted about 80 ms.

Install options come in three tabs: Plain OS, Control panel and Applications. I picked plain Ubuntu 26.04 LTS to see how much work the AI would take off my hands. A daily backup add-on is offered, but weekly backups are already included.

In a recent development, the five-minute estimate was about right. The “you’re ready” screen then gives you two ways in: the VPS dashboard, or a pre-filled ssh root@ command. It also offers a free domain for a year to use as the server’s hostname.

The overview demonstrates the OS, initiative, CPU, RAM, disk and bandwidth at a glance, with Docker Manager, Backups & Monitoring, Security and DNS Manager in the side menu.

Every server also gets a hostname under hstgr.cloud (mine was srvXXXXXXX.hstgr.cloud), which came in handy later for SSL. I’ve masked my hostname as srvXXXXXXX throughout and blurred IP addresses in the screenshots.

It has been revealed that plain Ubuntu doesn’t ship with Docker. Open Docker Manager in hPanel and it installs Docker for you with one click. From there you can deploy apps from a Compose file, a repository URL or the one-click catalog.

Click Web console and you’re logged in as root in a browser tab, with Hostinger Agent in a panel beside it. You don’t need an SSH client or keys. The login banner flagged 33 pending updates, 23 of them security fixes; more on that later. A quick docker --version confirmed Docker 29.9.3 was ready.

Here’s the whole app: a tiny HTTP server with a health check, and a Dockerfile on Node.js 24, a supported LTS line.

Then build it, run it and check it:.

It has been revealed that the build took 8.3 seconds, including pulling node:24-alpine, and the health check answered straight away. The --restart unless-stopped flag brings the container back after a crash or reboot, which I tested later.

That’s a working app, but on plain HTTP, on a high port, with no TLS. Getting it production-ready is the DevOps part I handed to the AI.

In a recent development, an AI-managed VPS isn’t the same as a traditional managed VPS. You still get a self-managed server with full root access, but Hostinger Agent does the work you’d normally do yourself. Agent (previously called Kodee) is an MCP-powered assistant that lives in the dashboard and beside the AI web terminal, and it’s included at no extra cost. You can also connect Claude or Cursor to your server through Hostinger’s MCP server.

I gave it three tasks in plain English.

My prompt: “Check that Docker is installed, then set up a reverse proxy with a free SSL certificate so my demo-app container (port 3000) is served at https://srvXXXXXXX.hstgr.cloud.”.

It started by looking around: the Docker and Compose versions, which ports were in use, whether a web server was already running, and the OS release. Then it installed Caddy from Caddy’s official repository, configured the proxy and made sure ufw allowed web traffic.

According to recent reports, it read Caddy’s logs to confirm the Let’s Encrypt certificate, which arrived in about 6 seconds. Finally it tested its own work: HTTPS returned 200, and plain HTTP returned a 308 redirect. The whole task took about two minutes.

Recent findings suggest that to give it a real fault, I ran docker stop demo-app and reloaded the site. Then I asked why it was returning a 502 and to fix it.

Industry observers note that in a single command, it checked the container state (Exited (137)) and searched Caddy’s logs, where it found connect: connection refused on port 3000. It restarted the container, confirmed /health and HTTPS were back, and even pointed to my docker stop in the terminal history. It also explained that --restart unless-stopped covers crashes and reboots, but not a manual stop.

A tip it didn’t mention: exit code 137 means Docker had to force-kill the container, because Node running as PID 1 ignores SIGTERM. Add --init to docker run for clean, instant shutdowns.

This was the most impressive answer. ufw already allowed only those three ports, but Agent noticed port 3000 was still reachable from the internet, because Docker-published ports bypass ufw rules.

It recreated the container bound to 127.0.0.1:3000, so the app is only reachable through Caddy, and confirmed with an external port check. It left DNS, time sync and Caddy’s local admin port running, explaining that stopping them would break DNS and time sync.

Then I asked it to reboot the server. First it checked that Docker and Caddy start on boot and that the container’s restart policy was set, then it rebooted. The site came back over HTTPS without any help from me.

Nothing I asked for was destructive, so Agent just got on with it: the firewall change, the container rebuild and the reboot all ran without a confirmation prompt.

The Agent panel claims so upfront, noting that terminal commands can run without one. For destructive actions such as reinstalling the OS or restoring a backup, Hostinger’s FAQ says Agent always asks for confirmation first.

One thing worth knowing: to close port 3000, Agent removed and recreated my container. That was harmless for a stateless demo, but a container that keeps data without a volume would lose it. Take a snapshot before big jobs, and keep the panel in view.

Here are the four intends at their Black Friday rates for a 24-month term.

For scale, here’s what my test used. With the Node app, Docker and Caddy all running, KVM 1 had 3.3 GB of its 4 GB RAM still available, and the app container itself used about 65 MB.

According to recent reports, so 4 GB is plenty for one or two small apps. Move to 8 GB on KVM 2 once you add Coolify, a database, or n8n with its own Postgres, because those are the services that eat memory.

Finding a cheap VPS got harder in 2026, because memory got expensive. AI data centres are buying up DRAM, and hosts are passing the cost on. In April 2026, Hetzner raised cloud server prices by up to 37%, citing hardware costs, then raised prices again in June. On the same April date, OVHcloud’s entry VPS went from $4.90 to $7.60, a 55% jump. Nobody can promise where VPS prices go next, but the trend this year has been up.

Recent findings suggest that this is how Hostinger’s Black Friday pricing works. You pay upfront for 12 or 24 months, and the 24-month term gives the lowest monthly rate. Your price is fixed for that whole term. After that, it renews at the standard rate.

On KVM 2, for example, you pay $210.96 today (the $8.79/mo rate) for 24 months, and it renews at $14.99/mo after that. Do the maths on the renewal before you commit, not just the headline rate.

My friend Sean Mullaney, the FI Tax Guy, recently published an interesting article about the potential downsides of annuities. One of his observations is so simple that I think it's easy to overlook:.

Most Americans already have an annuity. It's called Social Security.

It has been revealed that think about what an annuity is trying to accomplish. You give up some control over a pool of money in exchange for a predictable stream of income, often for the rest of your life. Social Security already provides lifetime income, with the added benefit of inflation adjustments.

For a married couple receiving substantial Social Security benefits, that could represent tens of thousands of dollars of annual income that they don't have to generate by selling investments.

  • Industry observers note that with the measure defeated, the license created by House Enrolled Act 1038 cannot be granted by the Indiana Gaming Commission.
  • Industry observers note that allen County, where developers were seeking to build, carried the most weight.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Voters in Allen, DeKalb and Steuben counties each rejected inland casino gambling by double digits on November 3. The single newly introduced license in House Enrolled Act 1038, tied to a project of at least $500 million, now has no county that can host it.

Industry observers note that with the measure defeated, the license created by House Enrolled Act 1038 cannot be granted by the Indiana Gaming Commission. A repeat ballot is also off the table. State law bars a second public question in any county that voted the measure down.

Industry observers note that allen County, where developers were seeking to build, carried the most weight. The county’s election-night summary counted 102,935 votes on the question, with 40.44% in favor. In DeKalb County, 7,374 voters stated no. Steuben County recorded 6,234 no votes.

The stakes were substantial. That minimum investment had to cover both the casino and its non-gambling amenities. At least 60% of that had to be spent within two years of the award. The license also carried a $150 million fee to the state, with $50 million of it going to a fund for former host communities hurt by casino closures.

It has been revealed that the projected public return was large as well. A study done for the Indiana Gaming Commission estimated that an Allen County casino could generate $204 million in revenue alongside its annual state tax payments. Under the act, 10% of the casino’s tax payments would have gone to the northeast Indiana regional development authority.

It has been revealed that the process hinged on the vote from the start. The commission’s July guidance said it would take applications only for a county or counties where voters approved inland casino gambling. None did.

In a recent development, gaming Commission officials said that with no county passing the referendum, nothing happens, and that any next steps are up to the legislature. That puts operators back in front of lawmakers.

In a recent development, lawmakers have already redrawn this map once. Instead of creating a new license, a January 22, 2026 committee version of House Bill 1038 would have relocated the Ohio County riverboat license. That inland casino could have gone to Allen, DeKalb, Steuben or Wayne County. The enacted version instead created one new license and eliminated one unused racino license. Indianapolis was kept off the list because a casino there would pull business from the existing casinos in Shelbyville and Anderson.

DeKalb and Steuben counties have turned away a casino in referendum votes. Allen County is still counting but 'no' is leading. https://t.co/rwMo6sIYZ2.

— Niki Kelly (@nkellyIN) November 4, 2026.

Recent findings suggest that the vote also lands in a state that is narrowing gambling elsewhere. House Bill 1052 lets the commission fine any operator or individual $100,000 for knowingly running an internet sweepstakes game in Indiana, starting July 1, 2026. Peer-to-peer skill-based poker is exempt. Indiana still has no legal online casinos.

Indiana was not alone on Election Day, as Nebraska voters also turned down a gambling expansion. In northeast Indiana, the act’s December 1, 2026 deadline for inland casino license applications now arrives with the commission taking no applications.

Breaking: Arkansas sues VGW and Kalshi, citing $66 million in VGW taxable sales in one year

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (647 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Readwrite

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin has sued sweepstakes casino operator VGW and prediction market Kalshi on the same day, alleging illegal gambling under state law.
  • According to recent reports, arkansas has opened a two-front legal fight against online gambling it says is unlicensed.
  • Both cases allege illegal gambling and violations of the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin has sued sweepstakes casino operator VGW and prediction market Kalshi on the same day, alleging illegal gambling under state law. The VGW complaint puts a dollar figure on the state's sweepstakes market and adds Arkansas to a growing list of states challenging the dual-currency model.

According to recent reports, arkansas has opened a two-front legal fight against online gambling it says is unlicensed. One lawsuit targets VGW, the tech giant behind Chumba Casino, LuckyLand and Global Poker. The other targets KalshiEX LLC and Kalshi Inc., the companies that own the Kalshi prediction market.

Both cases allege illegal gambling and violations of the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act. Both also include an unjust enrichment claim. In each case the state seeks restitution, penalties, taxes and injunctive relief.

Recent findings suggest that the VGW suit attacks the Gold Coin/Sweeps Coin model that almost every US sweepstakes casino relies on. It names ten affiliated VGW companies. The complaint says VGW reported about $66 million in taxable Arkansas sales between July 2025 and June 2026 and paid about $6 million in sales and use tax over that period, Gaming.net reported.

Those figures show a manufacturer declaring sales to the state and paying tax on them. Yet VGW holds no Arkansas casino license, the state alleges. The complaint also accuses VGW of letting 18-year-olds play, even though Arkansas casinos require players to be 21.

The case lands less than two months after the Newly introduced York settlement. New York Attorney General Letitia James declared that deal on September 9, 2026. It covered Chumba Casino, Global Poker and Luckyland Slots. VGW’s coin-based games were already off the table for New Yorkers by then, after her office sent the company a cease-and-desist letter in June 2025.

Kentucky Attorney General Russell Coleman went to court a few months earlier, claiming VGW’s sweepstakes casinos break Kentucky gambling law. Florida has also moved against dual-currency sweepstakes since June 2026. Arkansas now joins Kentucky, Florida and Newly introduced York on that list. For operators using the same coin structure, the pattern points to rising legal exposure state by state.

The Kalshi complaint rests on a constitutional definition. The Arkansas Constitution’s definition of casino gaming expressly covers accepting wagers on sporting events. Kalshi has never held a casino-gaming license from the state commission, the state alleges. Nor has it held any other Arkansas authorization to take sports wagers.

The complaint expressly limits itself to state-law claims and relief under Arkansas law. That choice means the state is relying on its own consumer-protection statute rather than waiting on the CFTC. Money lost, betting that gets out of hand, and depression or other damage to mental health are dangers Kalshi understands its customers face, Griffin’s office said.

Today I filed a lawsuit against VGW, an online gaming platform that features such games as @ChumbaCasino, LuckyLand Casino, @LuckyLandSlots, and @official_glp.

Arkansas’s gambling laws are clear. If you’re providing a means for Arkansans to gamble money within our state, you are… pic.twitter.com/qs2dhRMC8K.

— Attorney General Tim Griffin (@AGTimGriffin) November 4, 2026.

According to recent reports, filing both cases on the same day signals how Arkansas views the two products. The attorney general is treating sweepstakes casinos and sports event contracts as the same kind of unlicensed gambling. Other states may weigh whether to copy that approach.

The VGW case was filed in White County Circuit Court. The Kalshi case was filed in Independence County Circuit Court.

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

Weekly. Free. One click to leave.

Sources indicate that 7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

Sources indicate that A short clip can help a project in different ways. It can show an idea you have not filmed, put an existing design in motion, or give an announcement something to look at. The same approach will not work if the clip needs to demonstrate a real feature or show exactly what happened. Before choosing a generator, decide what the viewer needs to learn from the shot.

Sources indicate that this article uses Kling 4.0 as a worked example, but the decision process applies to any AI video generator. It covers how these tools turn prompts and images into video, how Kling 4.0 and a few alternatives differ, how to choose a starting mode, how to add exact text and branding outside the generated clip with a short ffmpeg script, and when real footage is the better choice. Feature details come from each vendor’s own pages at the time of writing and change often, so confirm current terms before you blueprint a production.

Recent findings suggest that ● Generated video is best for imagined shots. It suits concepts, backgrounds and early explorations, not instructions or faithful records.

Sources indicate that ● Your starting material decides the mode. A written idea, a reference image or a pair of opening and closing frames each call for a different input.

● Keep exact wording out of the generated clip. Titles, dates and logos belong on separate layers in an editor.

Industry observers note that ● Tools differ on control, cost and licensing. Compare inputs, length, resolution, credits and terms before you commit.

According to recent reports, ● Always review. Watch the whole clip at its final size and check it against the real product or design.

It has been revealed that most current systems extend diffusion models across time. A model learns to turn noise into a coherent set of frames guided by a prompt, and sometimes by an image or a clip. The research paper Video Diffusion Models describes this extension from images to video. The practical consequences are easy to observe.

● The prompt describes change over time. One visible change and one camera instruction usually work better than a long list of actions.

Sources indicate that ● Reference material steers but does not lock. A picture can suggest shape and colour without guaranteeing an exact match.

Industry observers note that ● Longer clips give more room for drift. Faces, logos and fine text are the first things to change between frames.

Industry observers note that ● Cost grows with length and resolution. Most hosted tools charge credits per second, so short previews are cheaper than full shots.

If you only have an idea, start with text. For a short announcement, you might ask for a band of light to move across a wall of coloured tiles. No one needs to recognise a particular wall, so the model can decide how it looks. Give it one visible change and a clear view of the subject. A prompt such as Soft morning light travels slowly across a wall of blue ceramic tiles. Fixed camera, no lettering is enough to see whether the idea works.

If you already have an illustration or a photo, reference mode gives you another starting point. Suppose you want a short concept clip for a desk accessory that only exists as a drawing. The picture can show the general shape and colour while the prompt describes the view you want. A video reference can help when it is the motion that is hard to explain, such as a slow camera slide. Say what each asset is meant to guide, and do not add a clip just because you have one.

Use keyframes when a particular view matters at a particular moment. Start with an opening image. If a short reveal also needs to end with the object facing forward, add an ending image to show that view. That is different from a reference image that mainly shows what the object looks like. Neither method guarantees an exact match, so check the result rather than assuming the uploaded picture has locked the design.

No single tool fits every project. The table summarizes what each option’s own page states, and “not stated” means the page did not say, not that the feature is absent.

Reading the table: hosted studios such as the one on JXP are the quickest way to test an idea and need no setup, but you pay per second and work within their supported inputs. Kling’s own site is the place to check announcements and API options directly, since its page says little about durations or resolution. Runway positions its models for motion quality and prompt following, while Google’s Gemini API video documentation suits teams building generation into their own products. The Diffusers video guide covers open-source pipelines for developers who want local control and are ready to manage GPUs and licences.

Trying an idea before making it. An illustrator might want to see how an imagined landscape feels when the light changes. A quick clip gives the team something to discuss: is the change visible, and does it happen at the right pace? It does not need to be the final animation to answer those questions.

It has been revealed that showing a product concept. A rotating view or a slow camera move can help people discuss how a design might be presented. It is useful early, when the shape and lighting are still being explored. Once the clip represents a product someone can buy, the standard changes. If a port moves or a button appears that the real product does not have, it is the wrong clip for that job.

Making a short visual for a post. A few seconds of moving colour can give an event announcement or a project update a distinctive opening. Put the name, date and other exact wording in your editor so they are readable and easy to change. The background only needs to support the message. If it competes with the text, use less movement or keep the background still.

Generated video is unreliable at lettering, so add titles in an editor or with a script. The command below overlays a title on a generated background and then checks the file properties. It assumes you already have a clip named background.mp4 and ffmpeg installed.

-vf "drawtext=text='Launch Night | 12 March':fontcolor=white:fontsize=64:x=(w-text_w)/2:y=(h-text_h)/2:box=1:boxcolor=black@0.35:boxborderw=24" \.

-c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -an announcement.mp4.

ffprobe -v error -select_streams v:0 \.

-show_entries stream=width,height,r_frame_rate,duration \.

-of default=noprint_wrappers=1 announcement.mp4.

Sources indicate that because the text lives in the command, you can reuse the same background for three events by changing one string. The font may need to be set with a fontfile option on some systems. This is the practical version of keeping the moving background in one file and the editable details in another.

If people will follow the clip as instructions, use real footage or a screen recording for the steps. A convincing shot of an app is not proof that a button is in the right place. A generated close-up of a product is not a reliable way to show how its parts fit. You can still use an imagined opening, but make the switch to the real demonstration clear.

It has been revealed that think about revisions, too. If your team expects to adjust the same title, logo or date every week, put those elements on separate layers in an editor. And if the only movement you need is a slow zoom on an approved picture, apply that zoom directly. There is no reason to risk changing the picture when a simple edit will do.

Industry observers note that this matters when someone else will maintain the video. A reusable announcement template is easier to hand over if the moving background is one file and the event details are editable. If the team likes the movement but needs three versions with different dates, they can reuse the same clip. If every change calls for a new generation, the time you saved on the first version may disappear on the second.

Recent findings suggest that the Kling 4.0 video generator on JXP currently offers 720p and 1080p settings and clip lengths from 3 to 30 seconds. According to its page, reference mode accepts up to 10 images and 5 videos, keyframe mode takes a first frame, middle frames and an optional last frame, and credits are charged per second with a higher rate at 1080p. For a first attempt, choose the frame shape you initiative to use and make the clip only as long as it needs to be. Check the displayed credit cost before generating, because a short preview can tell you whether the direction works before you spend on a longer shot.

Decide what a good result looks like before you generate it. For the tile background, you need to see the light move without distracting from the words you will add. For a product concept, check whether the shape stays recognisable as the viewpoint changes. Watch the whole clip at the size the audience will see it. If the shot misses the point, revise one thing at a time: the motion, the framing or the source image.

According to recent reports, ● Read the licence. JXP’s page lists a commercial use license on each plan and claims outputs are for creative and lawful use, with the user responsible for reviewing them. Other tools have different terms.

● Do not misrepresent products or events. A generated clip should not suggest features or footage that do not exist.

Sources indicate that ● Consider provenance. C2PA is an open standard for Content Credentials that records where content came from and how it was edited, and some tools support it.

Recent findings suggest that ● Disclose where required. Follow platform and advertising rules on labelling AI-generated or altered content.

● Fine text, logos, hands and fast motion can drift or flicker between frames.

● Reference images and keyframes steer the result but do not guarantee an exact match.

● Vendor specifications, such as resolution and length, can differ between a model announcement and a particular platform.

● Credit costs and plan terms change, so check them on the day you generate.

● Long or exact sequences are often cheaper and safer to film than to generate.

Short imagined shots, concept clips and moving backgrounds, where some details can be left open and the clip is reviewed before use.

Use text when you only have an idea, reference mode when you have a picture or clip to guide the look, and keyframes when specific views matter at specific moments.

Not reliably. Use real footage or a screen recording for instructions and demonstrations.

No. Hosted studios, vendor sites, developer APIs and open-source pipelines all exist. Compare supported inputs, length, resolution, cost and licensing against your project.

Recent findings suggest that kling 4.0 is a good candidate when the missing piece is an imagined shot and you can describe what it needs to do. Pick one such shot, try it, and put it next to the material you already have, and compare at least one alternative before you commit. If the project needs exact instructions or a faithful record, use the real thing. A useful first result is one that does its job in the edit, not simply one that looks impressive on its own.

Recent findings suggest that fanDuel's US adjusted EBITDA nearly disappeared in the third quarter of 2026, even as US revenue rose 6%. Flutter blamed spending on FanDuel Predicts and its Alberta launch, while FanDuel Casino's revenue growth slowed to 8%.

Recent findings suggest that fanDuel’s US business barely turned a profit in the third quarter of 2026. US adjusted EBITDA came in at just $3 million, against $51 million a year earlier. Revenue moved the other way, climbing 6% to $1.455 billion. Flutter blamed spending on FanDuel Predicts and its launch in Alberta.

For the regulated US market, the result shows how much prediction-market spending is costing one of its online leaders. The parent tech giant also lowered its full-year outlook for 2026. Buybacks are on hold for the foreseeable future so Flutter can focus on organic investment and paying down debt. Leverage stood at 4.6x at the end of the quarter, up from 3.7x in December 2025.

In a recent development, the group’s net loss widened to $1.148 billion from $789 million a year earlier. That figure includes impairments tied to Brazil, where Flutter stopped operating on Sept. 26, 2026.

FanDuel Casino is adding players much faster than it is adding revenue. Flutter pointed to competition and to slower growth as US iGaming states mature. The contrast with late 2025 is sharp. In the fourth quarter of 2025, FanDuel Casino grew revenue 33% and held 28% of US iGaming gross gaming revenue.

Recent findings suggest that flutter put that share at 27% for the three months to Sept. 30, the same level it reported for the second quarter. An outside estimate is lower. FanDuel’s iGaming share was 25.1%, down from 26.6% a year earlier, according to Citizens figures published by NEXT.io. The same figures indicated US iGaming growth slowing to 12% year over year in the third quarter, the lowest on record.

Sportsbook revenue grew 4%. FanDuel’s share of US sportsbook gross gaming revenue slipped to 36%, from 39% in the second quarter. Its share of handle was 33%.

The product drawing the investment is gaining people. Trading volume on FanDuel Predicts rose 102% from the prior quarter to $119 million. CEO Dan Taylor mentioned the app had 140,000 active users in October.

Flutter reiterates $50m prediction market revenue target for 2026:.

Flutter's FanDuel Predicts reached 140,000 active consumers in October as its parent maintained its $40m adjusted EBITDA forecast for market-making.

In a recent development, alberta is the other fresh cost. FanDuel reached more than 20% of the gaming market there in its first quarter. Management remarked that was well ahead of its pace after launching in Ontario.

Recent findings suggest that together, the figures are consistent with a firm trading near-term US profit for growth in newer markets and products. Taylor took over as CEO from Peter Jackson on Oct. 1, 2026. Buybacks will stay paused until leverage falls to a range of 2 to 2.5 times, a target he set for a period of about 24 months.
